The modal frame is a `+-----+` box whose `-` run has a visible gap at every cell boundary and whose `|` sides do not meet the `+` corners; it reads as 1990s ASCII art beside the rest of the UI. The `dismiss ✕`->`x` fallback reads as a lowercase letter at the end of the banner rather than a close control.

Compare mail-truecolor-dark.png, where `│` draws a continuous unbroken rule. Both are faithful to the token table; the question is whether ANSI-16 should be dropping Unicode at all, since a 16-colour TERM on a modern emulator still has box-drawing.

expected: Design language §7's degrade table assigns a distinct non-colour channel to unread, selected, focused and error only. Pass-2 plan decision 7 renders SY-5's four states with colour alone: "`synced` (dim, fgMuted) ... `offline` (warn), `backing off · retry 12s` (warn)". The reference is silent on what carries offline once warn's colour is gone.
actual: In NO_COLOR the whole distinction reduces to dim-versus-normal weight: `Synced` is SGR 2, `Offline` is plain. It is a real difference, but only by comparison against a state the user cannot see at the same time, and there is no absolute cue. Offline is arguably the most consequential state in the shell and it gets less signal than error's dedicated `!` gutter. ANSI-16 is fine here — SGR 93 at 8.33:1 is emphatic.
evidence: mail-offline-nocolor.png status row right: `Offline` ink rgb(216,222,233) = 9.63:1, normal weight. mail-nocolor.png same position: `Synced` ink rgb(144,149,158) = 4.32:1, dim. Nothing else differs — no marker, no reverse, no bold. mail-offline-truecolor-dark.ansi carries `38:2:212:179:106` warn, which is the entire signal at full colour.

capture: coverage gap across the whole sketch group
expected: The grading brief asks whether ANSI-16 "maps roles to sane slots on both grounds", and design language §7's degrade table names four channels: "unread = the `●` marker, selected = reverse video, focused = the edge bar's glyph weight (`▌` focused, `▏` unfocused ...), error = the `!` gutter marker alone. The UX-7 golden asserts no two states share a marker."
actual: Two coverage holes, neither a defect in what shipped but both limits on what this gate can certify. (1) There is no ANSI-16 or NO_COLOR capture on a light ground — the manifest declares the whole sketch group "kitty dark", and sizes.txt lists light variants for truecolor only. DG-1's failure mode is specific to bright-black-on-dark and would likely invert on a light ground, so ANSI-16's light behaviour is untested in both directions. (2) Three of the degrade table's four channels are unexercised by pass 2: no capture in any profile contains `●`, `▌`, `▏` or an `!` gutter, because the shell has no list rows and no error state. Only selection (the modal's answer pill) and the ground-step substitution are actually exercised here.
evidence: grep for `▌`, `▏` and `●` across every truecolor sketch .ansi returns nothing; the only selected element in the group is `  n stay  ` in modal-confirm. sizes.txt has mail-truecolor-light through short-truecolor-light but no *-ansi16-light or *-nocolor-light rows. The UX-7 golden's no-two-states-share-a-marker claim therefore rests on the golden, with no painted evidence at this gate.
